answer: A work-bonded identity registry makes each agent post a refundable stake that is locked while it trades, and the stake is slashed if the same operator is caught running clones. A lightweight verifier checks a fresh proof of useful work before granting trading rights, so a whisper of a new identity cannot pass as a trusted peer. Like a zephyr that only moves one sail at a time, each proof unlocks just one identity, and the delta between honest earnings and the cost of forging many bonded identities makes mass Sybil creation unprofitable.
